name: Royal Enfield India
description: Originally founded in Redditch, UK, and assembled by Enfield India in Madras from 1955. Revered across Delhi NCR and Punjab for its heavy-crankshaft 350cc and 500cc overhead-valve Cast Iron engines with separate pre-unit 4-speed gearboxes and right-side neutral finders.
key_technical_points: British Standard Cycle (CEI 26 TPI) fastener threads on chassis up to early 1970s.
Separate pre-unit gearbox requiring independent EP-90 gear oil and dry/semi-wet primary chaincase.
Dry-sump lubrication with dual reciprocating plunger oil pumps (feed & scavenge).

name: Yezdi & Jawa
factory: Ideal Jawa (India) Private Limited, Yadavagiri, Mysore
description: Built under Czechoslovakian license from 1960, later rebranded as Yezdi in 1973. Celebrated for its unique semi-automatic clutch release mechanism, dual exhaust ports, and rugged two-stroke engineering suited for Indian terrain.
key_technical_points: Semi-automatic clutch: gear shift lever simultaneously operates clutch release cam.
Combined kick-starter and gear shifter on a single co-axial shaft with push-and-rotate engagement.
Dual exhaust headers exiting into twin fluted chrome silencers.

name: Rajdoot (Escorts)
factory: Escorts Limited Motorcycle Division, Faridabad, Haryana
description: The quintessential North Indian utilitarian two-stroke workhorse. Built by Escorts in Faridabad under Polish SHL M11 license. Legendary for its Earles-type leading-link front suspension, unbreakable 173cc single engine, and the iconic 'Bobby' GTS 175 runabout.
key_technical_points: Leading-link (Earles type) front forks providing plush damping over unpaved village roads.
3-speed constant-mesh transmission with heavy-duty wet multi-plate cork clutch.
Villiers-derived transfer porting with high low-end torque pull under heavy payloads.

name: Yamaha India (RX100 & RD350)
description: The undisputed high-revving legends of Indian two-stroke motorcycling. Escorts Yamaha introduced the blistering twin-cylinder RD350 in 1983 and the cult-classic RX100 in 1985 with authentic Japanese 7-port cylinder castings and Mikuni carburetors.
key_technical_points: Yamaha 7-port cylinder induction with 4-petal stainless/fiberglass reed valve block.
Autolube mechanical variable-displacement oil pump driven off crankshaft.
Early 1985-1988 batches feature 'Made in Japan' embossed crankcase halves and 1E7 barrels.

name: Bajaj Auto (Chetak & Super)
factory: Bajaj Auto Limited, Akurdi & Waluj, Pune, Maharashtra
description: 'Hamara Bajaj'—the defining mobility vehicle of urban and semi-urban India. Derived from Piaggio Vespa 150 Sprint tooling, featuring a direct-drive rotary valve two-stroke engine, 4-speed hand twist shifter, and solid pressed-steel monocoque chassis.
key_technical_points: Rotary pad crankshaft timing dispensing with reed valves for zero maintenance.
Direct engine-to-rear-wheel transmission without secondary chain or belt drive.
Handlebar 4-speed twist grip gear selector utilizing twin push-pull cables.

name: Hero Honda Classics (CD100)
factory: Hero Honda Motors Limited, Dharuhera & Gurgaon, Haryana
description: 'Fill It, Shut It, Forget It'—the machine that ushered in India's modern 4-stroke commuter revolution in 1985. The Japanese Honda OHC horizontal cylinder engine with cast-iron sleeve and Keihin carburetor delivered legendary 80+ km/l fuel economy.
key_technical_points: Horizontal cylinder layout with overhead camshaft (OHC) driven by DID silent timing chain.
Pressure-fed trochoid oil pump providing pressurized lubrication to cylinder head and camshaft.
Early 1985-1991 engines feature 'Honda Motor Co Japan' embossed crankcase covers.

name: Classic Triumph
description: The quintessential British twin. The 360-degree parallel-twin engine with twin Amal carburetors delivered unmatched top speed and racing pedigree at the Isle of Man TT and Daytona.
key_technical_points: CEI (26 TPI) on early cycle parts, transitioning to UNF/UNC after 1969.
Lucas RM21 encapsulated alternator charging systems with Zener diode heat sinks.
Girling 315mm / 325mm stepped preload shock absorbers.

name: Norton
description: Pioneered the rubber-buffered Isolastic frame system, isolating heavy parallel-twin vibrations from the rider while preserving razor-sharp handling.
key_technical_points: Isolastic rubber mounts require precise clearance shimming (0.010" tolerance) to prevent high-speed weave.
Roadholder telescopic front forks with internal two-way hydraulic damping.
Superblend NJ306E barrel-shaped roller main bearings on crankshaft.

name: BSA
description: The Birmingham Small Arms company created the iconic Gold Star—the supreme high-compression single cylinder clubman racer of the 1950s.
key_technical_points: Dry-sump lubrication with high-pressure oil pump relief valve in timing chest.
Heavy 6-spring clutch setup engineered to handle high torque without slippage.
Whitworth (BSW) and British Standard Fine (BSF) fasteners across aluminum engine casings.

name: Honda CB Classics
description: The machine that coined the term 'Superbike'. The CB750 Four paired transverse 4-cylinder smoothness, electric start, and front hydraulic disc brakes.
key_technical_points: Dry-sump lubrication with separate oil tank in right-hand side cover.
4-into-4 exhaust system with staggered baffle cones.
Dual contact breaker points timed to 1-4 and 2-3 cylinder pairs.

name: BMW Motorrad Classic
description: The benchmark for long-distance durability and touring refinement. Horizontally-opposed boxer twin with shaft drive, Earles leading-link front forks, and Bing constant depression carburetors.
key_technical_points: Enclosed shaft drive with spiral-bevel ring and pinion final drive gears.
High camshaft located below crankshaft running in pressure-fed sleeve bearings.
Bosch 12V 280W alternator with diode board.

name: Moto Guzzi
factory: Mandello del Lario, Lake Como, Italy
description: The legendary 90-degree transverse V-Twin with longitudinal crankshaft and shaft drive. Famous for high-speed motorway stability and unmistakable exhaust cadence.
key_technical_points: Carcano-designed 90° V-Twin with gear-driven camshaft between cylinders.
Brembo integral triple-disc braking system linked to foot pedal.

name: Ducati Meccanica
description: Engineered by maestro Fabio Taglioni, famous for its bevel-gear driven camshafts and desmodromic valve actuation eliminating valve float at high RPM.
key_technical_points: Bevel gear shaft tower driving camshafts with micro-shim backlash adjustment.
Desmodromic valve operation: mechanical cam closing arms replace traditional valve springs.

name: Lambretta (Innocenti & API)
description: The iconic tubular-spine Italian scooter adapted and manufactured across India by Automobile Products of India in Mumbai and Scooters India in Lucknow.
key_technical_points: Tubular steel spine frame with enclosed shaft/chain transmission.
Direct piston-port induction with 4-speed handlebar grip selector cable assembly.

name: Matchless & AJS
description: Associated Motor Cycles (AMC) heavyweight singles and twins. Renowned for their heavy forged flywheels, 'Teledraulic' front forks, and unbreakable wet/dry sump engine architectures.
key_technical_points: Teledraulic hydraulically damped front suspension with external duplex springs.
Lucas magneto ignition with manual handlebar advance/retard lever.

name: Harley-Davidson Classic
description: WWII military flathead 45ci V-twins and post-war Servi-Cars preserved in classic collections across Delhi and Mumbai.
key_technical_points: Sidevalve (Flathead) valve-in-block design with low compression for low-octane fuel.
Hand gear shift on left side of fuel tank with foot rocker clutch pedal.

name: LML Vespa India
factory: Lohia Machines Limited, Panki, Kanpur, Uttar Pradesh
description: Formed as a joint venture with Piaggio of Italy in 1983. Produced the iconic LML Vespa 150 NV, Select, Star, and T5 with 5-port cylinder blocks, 12V electronic CDI ignition, and modern reed-valve engines.
key_technical_points: 5-port scavenge transfer induction for higher top speed and smoother mid-range torque.
12V 80W electronic CDI ignition eliminating breaker points.
Flat-profile cruciform 4-speed sliding selector cross.

name: Kinetic Honda India
factory: Kinetic Engineering & Honda Motor Co. Japan, Pithampur, Madhya Pradesh
description: Revolutionary 1984 joint venture that brought Japan's Honda Lead NH90 technology to India. Pioneered electric start, push-button ease, automatic continuously variable transmission (CVT), and auto-choke.
key_technical_points: Centrifugal dry clutch with V-belt variator transmission (no manual gearshifting or clutch lever).
12V Mitsuba high-torque electric starter motor with automatic Bendix pinion.
Automatic wax-pellet thermal auto-choke Keihin slide carburetor.
